content:
As an exercise to get used to Lean 4, I proved that π is transcendental. The code can be found here.

I proved it because it was in the list of missing theorems among the 100 theorems. I am not sure if it is significant for the community - maybe proving the generalized Hermite-Lindemann would only be?

As a beginner, I welcome any kind of comments or suggestions!
Welcome! I believe the list of 100 theorems includes proofs in repositories downstream of Mathlib (for e.g., number 5, 24, 67), so it would be appropriate to open a PR to record your formalization.

maybe proving the generalized Hermite-Lindemann would only be

there is indeed an open PR that proves a more general theorem, and has "pi is transcendental" as a corollary
#mathlib4 > Direct proof of the transcendence of π

Great to see that I've re-invented wheels, as I expected :)
If somebody else has already worked on it, I feel I do not deserve being credited as the "prover."
(It's a shame that I started this project one month ago, and another post taking exactly the same path was just out ten days before my post, though... LOL)

Re-doing proofs is a great way to learn IME!

That said, I think it would be nice to keep the documentation about the statuses of the 100 theorems more up to date, for e.g. if someone wanted to read a proof (not necessarily in Mathlib) that pi is transcendental
